standard_prerequisites.name: Alternation number of a hypergraph
standard_prerequisites.statement: For the cyclic group Z_r, a vector of nonzero entries is alternating when consecutive nonzero terms differ, alt(X) is the length of the longest alternating subsequence, and alt_r(H) is the minimum over injective orderings sigma of V(H) of the largest alt(X) for which no colour class spans an edge of H; the article's own definitions are retained at source lines 137-155.
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the invariant |V(H)|-alt_r(H) that both the counted theorem and its proof use, and the identity alt_r(H~) = alt_r(H) at source line 218.

standard_prerequisites.name: Cited alternation-number lower bound for the Kneser chromatic number
standard_prerequisites.statement: For every r >= 2 and every hypergraph H the chromatic number of the general Kneser hypergraph of H is at least the ceiling of |V(H)|-alt_r(H) divided by r-1; the article states this as Theorem alihaji at source lines 159-162 with its own citation to Alishahi and Hajiabolhassan. It is a cited result, not a claim of the counted theorem.
standard_prerequisites.use: Applied to the augmented hypergraph at source line 214 to get (r-1)|A| >= |V(H~)|-alt_r(H~).

standard_prerequisites.name: Admissible colour frequencies and matching colourings
standard_prerequisites.statement: An r-colour-frequency mapping assigns to each colour an integer below r; an (A,tau)-matching colouring colours the edges by colours of A so that every nonempty monochromatic matching has size at most the frequency of its colour, and the tau-matching chromatic number is the least size of a finite A admitting such a colouring (source lines 115-121).
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the objects and both conclusions of the counted theorem.

core_obligations: Fix an arbitrary finite colour set A of C admitting an (A,tau)-matching colouring c of H, since the first conclusion is asserted for every such A.

Build the augmented hypergraph H~ by adding r-1-tau(a) fresh vertices with their singleton edges for every a in A with tau(a) < r-1, and extend c to c~ colouring each new singleton edge by its own a (source lines 197-204).

Show that c~ is a proper vertex colouring of the general Kneser hypergraph of H~, because a monochromatic matching of colour a can use at most r-1-tau(a) of the new singleton edges and r of them would therefore give tau(a)+1 disjoint H-edges of colour a (source lines 205-212).

Apply the cited alternation-number lower bound to H~ and use the two identities (r-1)|A| = sum of tau over A + |V(H~)|-|V(H)| and alt_r(H~) = alt_r(H) to deduce that the sum of tau over A is at least |V(H)|-alt_r(H) (source lines 214-224).
Take the minimum over all finite A admitting an (A,tau)-matching colouring to obtain the stated bound on chi_M(tau,H) (source lines 225-228).

proof_roadmap.step: Fix an arbitrary finite A that admits an (A,tau)-matching colouring of H.
Augment H by singleton-edged dummy vertices and extend the colouring.
Show the extension is a proper vertex colouring of the general Kneser hypergraph.
Apply the cited Kneser lower bound and use the two identities for |V(H~)| and alt_r(H~).
Derive the frequency inequality and minimise over A.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is Theorem mainthmSaeed at source lines 168-176: for a tau-admissible hypergraph H it must produce a finite B with sum of tau over B at least |V(H)|-alt_r(H) and must bound chi_M(tau,H) by the minimum size of a finite A with sum of tau over A at least |V(H)|-alt_r(H). Its proof at source lines 194-230 is not adjacent to the statement: the author's remark at 178-186 and the pointer sentence at 192 sit in between, and the proof itself opens with the bold header Proof of Theorem mainthmSaeed at line 194. The argument augments H by r-1-tau(a) singleton-edged dummy vertices for every a in A (lines 197-204) and then has to show two things that are not routine: first that the extended colouring is a proper vertex colouring of the general Kneser hypergraph of the augmented hypergraph (lines 205-212), and second that the two quantities used in the count, (r-1)|A| = sum of tau over A + |V(H~)|-|V(H)| and alt_r(H~) = alt_r(H), both hold after the augmentation (line 218); the second identity is the delicate point, because the added singleton edges must not increase the alternation number. The deep topological input is the cited Alishahi-Hajiabolhassan bound restated at source lines 159-162 and is not re-proved here, so the counted material is rated H2 rather than H3.

compared.difference: The sibling card counts Theorem mainthmSaeed2, the equitable-colorability-defect bound ecd^r(H); the present card counts Theorem mainthmSaeed, the alternation-number bound |V(H)|-alt_r(H). The article proves them in two separate sections and records at source lines 285-292 that the two quantities are not comparable, each of the signs less, equal and greater occurring for suitable H, so neither statement implies the other; the proofs differ in the augmentation identity that has to be verified (alt_r(H~) = alt_r(H) at source line 218 against ecd^r(H~) >= |V(H~)|-|V(H)|+ecd^r(H) at source lines 328-335 of the sibling card).
